positive_controls.argument: Evidence-triggered planning identifies which horizon and dependent commitment a new result can legitimately revise, preserving necessary long-term intent while adapting near-term work.
The actual planning horizons, deadlines and switching costs identify when a learning result is useful and which unresolved premise threatens the next commitment.
Multihorizon planning places architectural learning before the relevant hard commitment while preserving long-lead dependencies that cannot be changed at iteration speed.
The plan horizon, decision deadline and feasible response define a discriminating investigation whose result can still inform an affordable revision.
The actual horizon and change cost locate where validation findings can alter scope, timing or assumptions without discarding necessary dependencies.
Multihorizon planning supplies the affected dependencies, available response horizon and switching costs for an empowered go, redirect, hold or stop decision.
Near-term planning identifies the next useful information and limits commitments until that information can inform the longer investment horizon.
Multihorizon replanning coordinates local iterations with longer integration and commitment dependencies instead of imposing one cadence on all work.
Evidence availability, horizon, switching cost and necessary dependencies explain when flexible replanning or a protected commitment interval is the proportionate control.
The actual decision horizon and response options determine when forecast changes matter to the plan and when switching costs justify waiting.
Multihorizon dependency and switching analysis identifies which revisions are cheap local responses and which expose costly commitments or delayed recovery.
